chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حُمَيْدُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ، عَن غَيْرِ وَاحِدٍ، عَن أَبَانٍ، عَن أَبِي بَصِيرٍ، عَن أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامِ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from more than one, from Aban, from Abu Basir, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: لَمَّا مَاتَتْ رُقَيَّةُ ابْنَةُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ: الْحَقِي بِسَلَفِنَا الصَّالِحِ عُثْمَانُ بْنُ مَظْعُونٍ وَأَصْحَابِهِ

translations.en: When Ruqayya, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), died, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Join our righteous predecessors, Uthman ibn Maz'un and his companions.

en.summary: This narration from Rijal al-Kashshi highlights the status of Uthman ibn Maz'un as a model of righteous solitude and devotion, often cited in Shia scholarship to illustrate the virtue of i'tikaf (spiritual seclusion) and independent worship. The Prophet's instruction for Ruqayya to join him underscores the continuity of spiritual lineage and the high regard for early companions who embodied piety outside the immediate family circle. This reference serves to validate the scholarly tradition regarding Uthman ibn Maz'un's unique spiritual standing among the Sahaba.
en.seo_question: Who did the Prophet Muhammad tell his daughter Ruqayya to join in the afterlife?

key_terms.عُثْمَانُ بْنُ مَظْعُونٍ: Uthman ibn Maz'un, a companion known for his piety
